anomalies.observed: In the 'WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES' block (sheet 1, region D) the Benewake LiDAR footprint PR4 is populated (no DNP/X mark) and its SCL/SDA pins are wired through header H3 onto NET0032/NET0008, the same nets that form the main non-isolated I2C bus (104/I2C_SDA, 105/I2C_SCL on M3A, the RTD M5, the H5/H6 headers and the ADM3260 primaries). PR4.VCC is tied to the +5V rail.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the LiDAR is documentation-only in the intended r2 design: 'its pins are "free" and it is marked on_board: no / excluded from the board; it is not wired into any net' (§1, §4.3, §6), and the wired water-level path is an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic sensor on two GPIOs (§4.4). The LiDAR should not be connected to the I2C bus.

evidence.quote: Water Height Sensor block: PR4 'LiDAR' pins VCC/SCL/SDA/GND/TX/RX; H3 pins carry red labels NET0032 and NET0008 (sheet 1, region D)
§4.3 'PR1 with on_board: no ... all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.'

anomalies.impact: An unmanaged, firmware-invisible I2C device is hung on the 3.3 V-pulled main I2C bus and powered at 5 V. This creates a 5 V/3.3 V logic-level mismatch on the bus and risks the device loading or holding SDA/SCL, which can corrupt or hang the pH/EC/RTD traffic; the intended ultrasonic water-level sensing is also absent from the board.

parsed.summary: The power train, feedback divider (52k3/10k -> ~5 V), I2C pull-ups (2.2 k), 110 m sense resistors, two ADM3260 isolators with a shared PDIS, the un-isolated RTD, the float interlocks and the crossed-out DNP sensors all match the intended design (reference-designator and auto-generated-net differences are non-anomalies). The one substantive deviation the drawing supports is that the LiDAR (PR4) is wired onto the main I2C bus and +5 V, whereas the specification's intended r2 design leaves it unconnected and uses an ultrasonic sensor for water level.
